description: Two-panel composite of calculated isoplethal phase diagrams for Fe–20Mn–Al–C alloys (reprinted from ref. [25]). Both panels share identical axes: "Weight percent Al" from 0 to 20 (ticks every 2) on x and "Weight percent C" from 0 to 5.0 (ticks every 0.5) on y; they differ only in temperature. (a) is the 900 °C section: a large γ field occupies the low-C/low-Al corner, with α + γ beneath it, α at high Al/low C, γ + κ in the centre, M3C + γ + κ and — in a narrow high-C band delineated by red lines — M3C + gra. + γ + κ ("gra." = graphite), plus M3C + γ near the left edge and Al4C3 + α + κ / α + κ at high Al. (b) is the 1200 °C section: γ, γ + κ, α + γ, α, Al4C3 + α + κ and α + κ persist, but liquid fields appear (L, γ + L, gra. + L + γ) and the κ-bearing fields shift. Experimental data symbols (open circle = γ, open triangle = γ + κ, filled square = α + γ, filled inverted triangle = α + κ, open square = γ + M…, plus open inverted triangles in (b)) are overlaid in both panels, sited mainly between the 6 and 16 wt% Al gridlines at low C; each symbol lies in the field matching its legend assignment, i.e. the calculated diagram reproduces the measured phase constitution.

subfigures.description: Calculated isoplethal phase diagram, weight percent C (0–5.0) vs weight percent Al (0–20), for Fe–20Mn–Al–C at 900 °C. Labelled fields: γ, γ + κ, M3C + γ + κ, M3C + gra. + γ + κ (red-bounded narrow band), M3C + γ, Al4C3 + α + κ, α + κ, α + γ, α. Legend: open circle = γ, open triangle = γ + κ, filled square = α + γ, filled inverted triangle = α + κ, open square = γ + M… (truncated). Experimental points plotted between about 3 and 16 wt% Al.

Same isoplethal section at 1200 °C. Fields: L, γ + L, gra. + L + γ, gra. + γ + κ, γ, γ + κ, Al4C3 + α + κ, α + κ, α + γ, α, plus a thin band adjacent to the C = 0 axis. Legend as in (a) with an additional open inverted triangle; right-edge legend text is cropped. Experimental points again fall in the corresponding fields.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a calculated phase diagram with x-axis labelled 'Weight percent Al' (0–20, ticks every 2) and y-axis labelled 'Weight percent C' (0–5.0, ticks every 0.5).
Panel (b) uses the same axis labels, ranges and tick spacing as panel (a).
Phase-field labels printed in (a) are: γ, γ + κ, M3C + γ + κ, M3C + gra. + γ + κ, M3C + γ, Al4C3 + α + κ, α + κ, α + γ and α.
The M3C + gra. + γ + κ field of (a) is enclosed by red boundary lines and forms a narrow high-carbon wedge near the left-centre of the diagram.
Liquid-bearing fields (L, γ + L, gra. + L + γ) appear in panel (b) but not in panel (a), marking the higher-temperature section.
Legend symbols in (a) are identified as: open circle = γ, open triangle = γ + κ, filled square = α + γ, filled inverted triangle = α + κ, open square = γ + M… (label truncated at the image edge).

In both panels experimental datum symbols are plotted chiefly between the 6 and 16 wt% Al gridlines and below about 2.5 wt% C, and each symbol sits inside the phase field matching its legend assignment.
The caption states the figure shows calculated phase diagrams of Fe–20Mn–Al–C alloys at (a) 900 °C and (b) 1200 °C, reproduced with permission from ref. [25], Copyright 2010, Elsevier.
The legend entries at the right-hand edge of both panels are cut off, so the exact phase names paired with the open-square (a) and additional inverted-open-triangle (b) symbols cannot be read.

The citing text asserts that the phase composition determined from experimental data is well represented by these calculated diagrams of Fe–20Mn–Al–C steel as a function of Al and C content (Figure 3a,b).
